# Preflight guide
`circleci preflight run` tests your working tree on CircleCI before you commit it.
It is built for coding agents: change code, preflight it, read the failures, fix, repeat.

## How it works

1. The working tree — committed, staged, unstaged and untracked, minus ignored
   files — is recorded as one commit whose parent is where HEAD forked from the
   remote's default branch, so its diff shows everything you are changing. A
   throwaway index is used, so HEAD, the index, the working tree and the stash
   are never touched. When nothing differs from the default branch, its commit
   is pushed as-is. If the default branch is unknown, the parent is HEAD.
2. The commit is pushed to `cci/preflight/<id>` on the remote (pre-push hooks are
   skipped). The project's push trigger starts a run for it; the project must build
   pushes to every branch.
3. The run is watched. Each failed job is reported once, as soon as it is seen.
4. At the first failed job the rest of the run is cancelled; with `--no-failfast`
   the whole run is awaited instead. Either way the branch is then deleted, unless
   `--no-cleanup` is passed. `circleci preflight cleanup` removes branches
   left behind.

## Detecting a preflight in config

Jobs see the branch name, so a step can skip work that should not run for
uncommitted code — deploys, publishing, slow optional suites:

```shell
if [[ "$CIRCLE_BRANCH" == cci/preflight/* ]]; then echo "preflight: skipping deploy"; exit 0; fi
```

A workflow can be filtered out entirely with `branches: { ignore: /^cci\/preflight\/.*/ }`.

## Event stream

With `--json`, stdout carries one JSON object per line and nothing else. Every
object has a `type`:

- `branch_pushed` — `preflight_id`, `branch`, `commit`, `base` (the commit's parent),
  `base_branch` (empty when `base` fell back to HEAD) and `changes` (false when
  nothing differed from `base` and `commit` is `base` itself).
- `run_started` — `run_id`, `project`, `branch`, `commit`, `url`.
- `job_failed` — `job`: `id`, `name`, `workflow_id`, `workflow`, `url`,
  `failed_steps[]` (`execution`, `num`, `name`, `exit_code`), `failed_tests[]`
  (`classname`, `name`, `message`; at most 25) and `failed_test_count`.
- `run_summary` — always last: `run_id`, `outcome`, `ended`, `duration_ms`,
  `url`, `errors[]` (`type`, `message`), `failed_jobs[]` (`id`, `name`, `workflow`,
  `url`), `run_cancelled`, `branch_deleted` and `cleanup_error`.

`outcome` is `succeeded`, `failed` or `canceled` once the run has ended; `failing` when the
preflight stopped at the first failed job; `timed_out` or `interrupted` otherwise.
Test results are read when the job fails, so a job whose results are still being
processed may report no tests.

Exit codes: 0 succeeded, 1 failed, 3 auth error, 4 API error, 5 no run started,
6 cancelled or interrupted, 7 config error, 8 timed out.

## Acting on failures

For each `job_failed` event, start from `failed_tests` when present, otherwise from the
failed step's output: `circleci job output get <job.id> --step-num <num>`. Once the
summary arrives, `circleci run get <run_id> --failure-report` prints every failed
step's condensed output. Fix the code and run the preflight again.


## Examples
### Stream events and keep only failures
`$ circleci preflight run --json | grep '"type":"job_failed"'`

### Remove preflight branches left behind
`$ circleci preflight cleanup`
